title: Family Staying On Your Own Side Foster Chance
author: Chance, Foster
summary: Foster Chance distinguishes three related but different concepts: loving yourself (a feeling of warmth and willingness to forgive), trusting yourself (believing your perceptions and judgments matter), and honoring yourself (what love looks like in action — keeping faith, keeping promises, behaving like the best friend you can imagine). Honoring requires both truth and loyalty simultaneously: loyalty without truth is delusion, truth without loyalty is betrayal. The central trap for people who want to do good: the very decency that makes you especially good to others may keep you from being good to yourself. Five ways we abandon ourselves: taking the group's side instead of our own; believing we are our failures or achievements; living in fear (which mistakes ego threat for body threat); mistaking rumination for contact with what is; failing to govern attention and energy. Achievement particularly misleads — it can come from panic or dissociation as easily as from self-understanding. The final call: inhabiting your own life so fully that your whole, complete self is actually present in it.
points: Honoring yourself requires truth AND loyalty simultaneously — loyalty without truth is delusion, truth without loyalty is betrayal; honoring is both at once plus a promise.
The trap: the very decency that makes you especially good to others may keep you from being good to yourself — a life of service can become a life of making yourself small.

Achievement misleads: 'what looks like effortless drive from the outside is often panic on the inside' — achievement can come from luck, dissociation, or overriding fear, not only from genuine self-understanding.
Rumination disguises itself as inner work but is not contact with what is — the test is whether it leads anywhere toward a truer view, a quieter mind, or an experiment in doing something different.
The greatest gift: inhabiting your own life so fully that your whole, complete self is actually present in it.
quotes: To honor yourself is what that love looks like in action: keeping faith with what is true and important to you, keeping promises to yourself; being kind to the person you were.

Loyalty without truth is delusion. Truth without loyalty is betrayal. Honoring is both at once, plus a promise: I will stand up for you, keep promises to you, understand and explain how you were feeling and thinking, have love and compassion for you, and tell you when you are misguided and can do better.
That is the trap: the very decency that makes you especially good to others may keep you from being good to yourself.

Achievement that is not in service to honoring ourselves — to becoming the fullest expression of who we are — is in service to something else: safety, status, quieting an old fear. And that can make the inner work even harder.
You are not your accomplishments, however proud of them you may be. You are not an object, a fixed thing you use for a purpose. You are a being, and your proper 'mode' is becoming.
Rumination is not moving anywhere; introspection is different. The test is whether it leads anywhere — toward a truer view, a quieter mind, or an actual experiment in doing something different.
In the end, staying on your own side is just this: inhabiting your own life so fully that you — your whole, complete self — are actually present in it.
